subject: Inference economics — scope alignment & technical asks
messages:
From: jasmine_liu@redwood.com
To: Samir Gupta <samir@finlytics.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Inference economics — scope alignment & technical asks

Hi Samir / Priya —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap from our side so we’re all aligned on pain, success criteria, and immediate asks. I’ve kept this intentionally concise so you can reply to the bullets that need clarification.

Pain points you described
- Unit token cost is spiking as model usage grows (esp. late-stage generation for statements and long form reports).
- High tail latency causing timeouts for some customers; unpredictable throughput during peak batch jobs.
- Ops overhead from having to maintain multiple model variants and quantization experiments in-house.

Current stack (as you described)
- Inference served from a mixed fleet: a few committed GPUs on-prem + opportunistic cloud VMs for burst; internal autoscaling is manual.
- Model variants: causal LLM v1.3 (fp16) for short chat, v1.3-large for report generation; experimenting with int8 quant locally.
- Redis-based prefix cache for per-session context, but cache hit rate for heavy reports is low (~12%).

Success criteria for a pilot (what would make this a win)
- 30–40% reduction in cost-per-1000-tokens for the report-generation workload without degrading P50/P95 latency beyond your limits.
- P50 latency for short chat <= 120ms; P95 tail for report-gen under 1.5s for the expected batch sizes.
- Clear operational playbook (batching/caching config, fallback model variants) that your SREs can adopt in 2–3 weeks.

Immediate asks / next steps we agreed
1) You to share: a small representative dataset (6–10 example requests per workload) + QPS profile for peak and off-peak (we’ll treat any shared data per the NDA).
2) We’ll share: a proposed pilot scope template (attached) and a preliminary cost-sensitivity checklist (attached PDF).
3) Technical alignment call: propose Thurs 5/13, 10:00–10:45 PT — lab session to go over caching strategy and quantization openness (we’ll demo int8 vs 4-bit profiles).
4) Decision gate: after a 2-week PoC we’ll review metrics against the cost and latency targets above and propose Dedicated vs Hosted config based on results.

Questions for you (please reply inline)
- Which model variant is responsible for the majority of token spend today (v1.3-large or mix)?
- Are there regulatory constraints that would prevent sending sample requests to a hosted PoC versus requiring on-prem evaluation?
- Any hard requirements for embedding persistence / audit logs for the pilot?

Attachments: pilot-scope-template.xlsx (XLSX) — fill the highlighted cells and return; redwood-inference-cost-checklist.pdf (PDF)

Thanks — we’ll prep the lab environment if you confirm the dataset and the Thurs slot.

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
jasmine_liu@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123


From: Samir Gupta <samir@finlytics.com>

Subject: Re: Inference economics — scope alignment & technical asks

Thanks Jasmine — great summary. A few clarifications below.

- Majority of token spend is v1.3-large for report generation (~70% of tokens), the chat path is high volume but thin tokens per request.
- We can share the sample requests and QPS profile; prefer a hosted PoC for speed but we need assurance that the logs will not be retained beyond the PoC window — can you confirm retention policy?
- No special embedding persistence requirements for the pilot; audit logs for who queried which model would be helpful but GDPR/data residency is a consideration for EU customers (we are US-first, but have EU customers).

We can do Thu 5/13 10:00 PT. I’ll upload the sample requests to the Drive link you suggested and fill the pilot template by EOD Wed.

Samir

From: jasmine_liu@redwood.com
To: Samir Gupta <samir@finlytics.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 08:14:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Inference economics — scope alignment & technical asks

Samir — thanks for the fast reply, and for confirming the Thurs slot. Quick answers and what we’ll bring to the lab: 

- Retention: for Hosted PoC we’ll enable a strict 30-day ephemeral retention and we will scope a data-handling addendum (we’ll send language). If Hosted is not acceptable, we’ll spin a VPC/private PoC — will take ~48 hours more to provision.
- Audit logs: we can provide redacted query logs and an audit log stream for model calls scoped to the pilot — we’ll include that in the deliverables.

What we’ll demo in the lab (agenda for 45 min)
1) Baseline run on your sample dataset (we’ll show per-token cost and latency breakdown).
2) Caching changes: prefix cache tuning + KV cache for 1:1 report reuse — expected uplift estimates.
3) Batching profiles for report-gen: show throughput improvements and CPU/GPU utilization at different batch sizes.
4) Quantization matrix: int8 vs 4-bit performance and quality tradeoffs (we’ll show token-level quality diffs).

Proposed pilot success metrics (for the PoC readout) — please confirm or edit before Wed EOD:
- Cost: >=30% improvement on report-gen path measured as normalized cost-per-1k tokens.
- Latency: P50 chat <=120ms, P95 report-gen <=1.5s (measured at your peak QPS).
- Quality: BLEU-like/verifiable quality delta <=2% on your acceptability metric; human review sample to validate.

Next steps checklist (our side)
- Send PoC environment link + short runbook (by EOD Wed) — marissa will own operations touchpoints.
- Prep int8/4-bit quant profiles for the lab.
- Share retention addendum draft.

If any of the success targets are unrealistic we should set a lower bar for the lab and keep the 30% cost reduction as a stretch target — call that out if needed.

See you Thu.

—Jasmine

From: Samir Gupta <samir@finlytics.com>

Subject: Re: Inference economics — scope alignment & technical asks

Sounds good — we’ll upload the dataset to the Drive link and Priya will fill the template. 30-day retention for the Hosted PoC is acceptable for now — if we need longer we’ll escalate.

One small ask: please include a short section in the runbook about how you’ll measure and attribute token cost (we track internal charges per model variant). Also add a note on canary/fallback behavior if a quantized model underperforms.

Thanks — see you Thu.

Samir
